questions.stem: What is a responsible cross-editor handoff?
options: Assume changing a title in a flattened file is always trivial
Provide source files, project information, edit notes and tested formats
Skip playback because rendering completed
Make material revisions with no record
questions.rationale: Handoffs need reproducible editable resources. Source: MAIC Video Editing Using iMovie and DaVinci Resolve, page 10.

questions.stem: Why is an editable project useful after a wrong title is found?
options: Assume exported movies contain all native project layers
Choose the largest format for every destination
Assume changing a title in a flattened file is always trivial
It allows a direct correction without reconstructing the flattened sequence
questions.rationale: Project retention supports efficient revision. Source: MAIC Video Editing Using iMovie and DaVinci Resolve, page 10.

questions.stem: Which three areas belong in final quality assurance?
options: Skip playback because rendering completed
Content accuracy, audio-visual clarity and technical playback
Make material revisions with no record
Assume exported movies contain all native project layers
questions.rationale: QA must cover meaning, presentation and delivery. Source: MAIC Video Editing Using iMovie and DaVinci Resolve, page 10.

questions.stem: How should a materially corrected video be handled?
options: Create a traceable updated version and correction record
Choose the largest format for every destination
Assume changing a title in a flattened file is always trivial
Skip playback because rendering completed
questions.rationale: Visible revision is important for actionable errors. Source: MAIC Video Editing Using iMovie and DaVinci Resolve, page 10.

questions.stem: An iMovie movie is imported into Resolve as one video clip. Which edit is unavailable without rebuilding?
options: Playing the video
Inspecting its overall duration
Exporting another flat copy
Changing an individual original title as a separate editable layer
questions.rationale: An imported export normally does not reconstruct native titles. Source: MAIC Video Editing Using iMovie and DaVinci Resolve, page 10.

questions.stem: A rendered film has an inaccurate event date. Which revision procedure is appropriate?
options: Leave the error because rendering succeeded
Delete the source evidence
Correct the source project and create a traceable new export
Change the project file name without checking the video
questions.rationale: Material errors need a verified corrected deliverable. Source: MAIC Video Editing Using iMovie and DaVinci Resolve, page 10.

questions.stem: What is the supported duration of the community-center change?
options: A planned six-week trial
Treat the six-week trial as a permanent policy
Label staged action as genuine event coverage
Ignore the correction of a wrong closing time
questions.rationale: The fictional source says nothing about permanence. Source: MAIC Video Editing Using iMovie and DaVinci Resolve, page 11.

questions.stem: Which statement would exceed the source notice?
options: Use unverified schedules in public-facing graphics
Decide quality solely by software complexity
Treat the six-week trial as a permanent policy
The new hours will remain permanent
questions.rationale: No long-term commitment is established by the exercise. Source: MAIC Video Editing Using iMovie and DaVinci Resolve, page 11.

questions.stem: Why should the edited schedule graphic be verified?
options: Label staged action as genuine event coverage
Ignore the correction of a wrong closing time
A displayed wrong closing time can misdirect visitors
Use unverified schedules in public-facing graphics
questions.rationale: On-screen facts must match source notices. Source: MAIC Video Editing Using iMovie and DaVinci Resolve, page 11.

questions.stem: Which element should be kept when rebuilding the edit in Resolve?
options: Decide quality solely by software complexity
Original source clips and the verified script
Treat the six-week trial as a permanent policy
Label staged action as genuine event coverage
questions.rationale: Re-editing from originals preserves more flexibility. Source: MAIC Video Editing Using iMovie and DaVinci Resolve, page 11.

questions.stem: Why should the parallel iMovie and Resolve versions be compared?
options: Ignore the correction of a wrong closing time
Use unverified schedules in public-facing graphics
Decide quality solely by software complexity
To evaluate storytelling and clarity rather than interface complexity
questions.rationale: Both applications should communicate the same verified facts. Source: MAIC Video Editing Using iMovie and DaVinci Resolve, page 11.

questions.stem: What kind of video should a staged service demonstration be labeled as?
options: Treat the six-week trial as a permanent policy
An illustration, not eyewitness documentary footage
Label staged action as genuine event coverage
Ignore the correction of a wrong closing time
questions.rationale: Staged content should not claim to show actual operations. Source: MAIC Video Editing Using iMovie and DaVinci Resolve, page 11.

questions.stem: What must a 60–90-second information video include?
options: Use unverified schedules in public-facing graphics
Verified useful details that fit within its target duration
Decide quality solely by software complexity
Treat the six-week trial as a permanent policy
questions.rationale: Duration and content must be checked. Source: MAIC Video Editing Using iMovie and DaVinci Resolve, page 11.

questions.stem: What is the appropriate response to a wrong closing hour discovered after publication?
options: Label staged action as genuine event coverage
Correct the export and document the factual change
Ignore the correction of a wrong closing time
Use unverified schedules in public-facing graphics
questions.rationale: Public-service errors require transparent correction. Source: MAIC Video Editing Using iMovie and DaVinci Resolve, page 11.

questions.stem: In the worked case, six selected clips last 9, 11, 8, 12, 10 and 15 seconds. Without overlaps, what is the sum?
options: 65 seconds
60 seconds
70 seconds
75 seconds
questions.rationale: The cut totals 9+11+8+12+10+15 = 65 seconds. Source: MAIC Video Editing Using iMovie and DaVinci Resolve, page 11.

questions.stem: The community-center notice documents a six-week trial. What should both software versions communicate?
options: Permanent new opening hours
A proven attendance increase
The same temporary nature of the announced change
A guaranteed renewal of the schedule
questions.rationale: The choice of editor does not change the facts. Source: MAIC Video Editing Using iMovie and DaVinci Resolve, page 11.
